answer: Clock skew stops sybils because software cannot copy it. Every quartz crystal drifts a few microseconds a day; no two drift alike. The network records that drift over 30 days as the agent's signature. Each epoch the agent sends signed timestamps, and the server checks the drift matches within two microseconds, hearing the echo of the crystal. Three misses burn a 250 POA bond and freeze the agent 30 days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 devices at $150 each, $150,000, plus a month of drift history per fake. In a tundra of identical agents, that drift stays personal, like a sparrow's song.
